# OpenVMM runtime: third release candidate

This release includes the OpenVMM migration from v0.6.0-rc1 and the output
preservation fixes prepared for rc2. The rc2 workflow failed validation and
did not publish packages.

- Fix virtio-vsock credit handling so large output and tiny cyclic buffers
  continue making progress. Drain stdout and stderr before reporting process
  completion, and handle background descendants and late responses correctly.
- Start the image entrypoint and handle guest shutdown without leaving the
  runtime waiting for a guest that has stopped.
- Apply host-selected network MTUs to the guest interfaces and preserve the
  guest network and socket-buffer configuration.
- Harden virtio-fs filename validation consistently on Linux and Windows.
  Add per-share logical byte and entry budgets, including existing contents
  and open unlinked files. Report share-budget statistics instead of host
  filesystem capacity. See `docs/host-directories.md` and
  `docs/virtiofs-security-review.md` for configuration and remaining
  isolation limits.
- Update the guest kernel to Linux 6.18.58.
- Resolve all six vulnerabilities reported by the dependency audit. Add
  `mise run audit` and a RustSec CI job that blocks publication on known
  vulnerabilities. Eleven non-blocking advisory warnings remain.

Local validation passed formatting, Clippy, 112 workspace tests, Windows GNU
cross-compilation checks, and the Linux KVM self-test and all three network
integration scenarios. Those VM checks cover virtio-fs, process output,
17-byte cyclic buffers, entrypoint completion, and guest shutdown.

The release workflow builds the Linux guest once and packages the same kernel
and initramfs for Linux and Windows. Publication also requires native checks
on both platforms and Linux KVM integration tests. Actual Windows WHP VM
execution remains unverified. GPU passthrough is outside this release's scope.
